en.concept: Objects around us are made from different materials and have different properties. These properties can be used to group objects. Lustre, hardness, texture, solubility and transparency are important properties. Material properties also help in choosing materials for particular uses.

sections.title: Transparency and Uses
sections.concept: Transparent materials allow objects to be seen clearly. Translucent materials allow some light through but objects are not clear. Opaque materials do not allow light through.

examTraps.title: Object and Material
examTraps.fact: An object may be made from a material.
examTraps.confusion: Treating the object's name as the material name can be incorrect.

examTraps.title: Lustre
examTraps.confusion: A shiny object should not be identified as metal only from lustre.

examTraps.title: Dissolving
examTraps.fact: Sugar dissolves in water while sand does not.
examTraps.confusion: Not being visible in water does not always mean that a substance was destroyed.

examTraps.title: Transparency
examTraps.fact: Objects are seen clearly through transparent materials.
examTraps.confusion: Objects are not seen clearly through translucent materials.

examTraps.title: Hardness
examTraps.fact: Hardness and heaviness are different properties.
examTraps.confusion: A heavy object should not automatically be called hard.

examTraps.title: Classification
examTraps.fact: Classification depends on the selected property.
examTraps.confusion: The same object can be placed in different groups when different properties are selected.
